answer: A hosted agent economy prices Sybil attacks with a per-identity stake held for several epochs. Each identity posts a bond, and rewards go only to those that also clear a proof-of-work beacon check. Ten thousand puppets freeze ten thousand bonds as idle locked capital, and the withdrawal delay stops one bond being recycled across identities, so cost stays linear. Payouts split by real work, not identity count, so the fake fleet earns only a thin slice. Breaking even needs each forgery to out-earn its bond, so the voyage ends in failure with no shale of profit left.
